what_it_anchors: A three-tier KASP outcome chain in an autopolyploid: 77 SNPs selected, 49 genotyped in both parents, 24 in line with the genetic map (Supplementary Table 10); only the last tier is file-backed
claim: 77 > 49 > 24, strictly nested; 24 rows in sheet S10 of Table_1.XLSX; the workbook prints the allele primers with the SNP at the 5' end (3' base matches the allele in only 4 of 48 allele primers), so no 3'-allele axis may be assumed from it
claim_kind: primary table (supplement S10, assay rows); the 77 and 49 tiers are text-only
access_detail: only Table_1.XLSX was retrievable; the site's SupplementaryTables 8-10 .docx are 404 on every URL tried

citation: Vendramin V, Ormanbekova D, Scalabrin S, Scaglione D, Maccaferri M, Martelli P, Salvi S, Jurman I, Casadio R, Cattonaro F, Tuberosa R, Massi A. Genomic tools for durum wheat breeding: de novo assembly of Svevo transcriptome and SNP discovery in elite germplasm
what_it_anchors: TETRAPLOID vs HEXAPLOID on the same 90K array and the same 288-accession AABB panel: hexaploid-derived SNPs failed 4,782/73,647 (6.5%) and were polymorphic 20,807 (30.2% of non-failed); durum-derived SNPs failed 703/7,940 (8.8%) and were polymorphic 3,738 (51.7% of non-failed)
claim: the D genome's presence does not raise the no-call rate (6.5 vs 8.8%, the authors' t-test P = 0.235) but it lowers informativeness by ~1.7x in an AABB panel; both percentages use different denominators (failed = all assays, polymorphic = non-failed only)

what_it_anchors: NEGATIVE datapoint on the homeolog axis: in an AADD allotetraploid, 11 KASP assays were screened per assay (Table 3) with 8 usable (7 co-dominant, 1 dominant) and 3 unusable, on cluster separation alone, with no homoeolog step; two usable assays were designed from DIPLOID relatives (G. tomentosum, G. mustelinum) and used unre-designed on the AADD panel
claim: 8/11 usable by cluster separation (72.72% printed) with homeolog_handled = 'not stated'; the diploid-relative assays i60979Gt and i64854Gm were both GOOD, so mis-priming across the subgenome boundary was not the binding constraint in this system
